_comment: PARTIAL BASELINE. Thirteen of the seventeen harnesses still have NO recorded run and keep the original placeholder semantics: the real baseline for those is produced by an actual per-harness smoke run under clang-cl + libFuzzer on the self-hosted runner. See tests/security/fuzz/README.md - 'Why no live baseline is committed'. What changed in phase-73 is that the four signature harnesses DO now have a recorded clean run, so leaving the whole file at null would have understated what is known.
_provenance_warning: The four recorded entries come from a LOCAL run of build-fuzz-local (the /MT static-CRT build produced by build_fuzz_local.bat) on the developer workstation, NOT from a windows-fuzz.yml campaign. They are 60 s each, where the CI campaign is 1270 s. Do not quote them as CI results, and do not treat 'clean' here as evidence about the thirteen harnesses that were not run. The distinction is the whole point of recording provenance at all.

harnesses.name: fuzz_pkcs7_verify
harnesses.added: phase-73 (PROMOTION of the unlinked LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput in tests/test_pkcs7_fuzz.cpp - DCA 0037)
harnesses.surface: d2i_PKCS7 -> PKCS7_get0_signers -> PKCS7_verify, shared verbatim with the test_pkcs7_fuzz.cpp seed-replay oracle via tests/security/fuzz/pkcs7_fuzz_core.h
harnesses.coverage_caveat: 17 edges is LOW and is not a measurement error: the body is a thin wrapper over OpenSSL, and OpenSSL comes from vcpkg WITHOUT sanitizer or coverage instrumentation, so libFuzzer sees only PDFE's own edges and ASan sees only PDFE's own loads and stores. Coverage guidance and memory-error detection inside OpenSSL's ASN.1 parser are therefore WEAK for all four signature harnesses. Recorded as a named follow-up in docs/audit/meta-audit-2026-07/followup/phase-73-dispositions.md rather than left for a reader to infer from a small number.

harnesses.name: fuzz_tsa_response
harnesses.surface: TsaClient::verifyTimestampToken (RFC 3161 TimeStampToken DER, via OpenSSL TS_*)
harnesses.scope_caveat: Covers the TOKEN PARSE only. TsaClient's own transport paths (libcurl at TsaClient.cpp:210-236, WinHttp at :278-312) are NOT reached: parseTimeStampResp and httpPost are private, and driving them would mean widening the product's interface to suit a test. The HTTP layer is a named follow-up in the phase-73 disposition, not something this harness quietly counts as covered.
